The abdominal pain quickly resolved, and the platelet count and liver function improved within 1 week of starting acyclovir. The patient was subsequently discharged.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A patient with idiopathic membranous nephropathy on immunosuppressive therapy developed sudden onset intense epigastric pain on Day 77, which worsened by Day 79. Initial imaging on Day 79 showed mild fat tissue density increase around the celiac and superior mesenteric artery roots but ruled out other acute abdominal pathologies. On Day 80, characteristic varicella-like blisters appeared on the face and trunk. VZV infection was confirmed by skin lesion biopsy showing ground-glass nuclei and positive PCR for VZV, along with markedly increased blood VZV-DNA numbers. Intravenous acyclovir and immunoglobulin were administered, and immunosuppressants were reduced. The abdominal pain quickly resolved, and platelet count and liver function improved within 1 week of starting acyclovir, despite a temporary worsening of liver function and development of disseminated intravascular coagulation prior to improvement.
